summative_rubric.title: Fraction Street — Summative Rubric
summative_rubric.purpose: End-of-unit rubric covering all 7 expectations B1.1-B1.7.

rows.expectation_text: read, represent, compose, and decompose whole numbers up to and including 1000, using a variety of tools and strategies, and describe various ways they are used in everyday life

levels.descriptor: Reads numerals to 99; struggles with 3-digit numbers.
Reads to 1000 with prompts; misses zero placeholders.
Reads, builds, and decomposes numbers to 1000 with the standard expanded form.
Produces multiple flexible decompositions; volunteers real-life uses for 3-4 digit numbers.

rows.expectation_text: compare and order whole numbers up to and including 1000, in various contexts

levels.descriptor: Defaults to ones-first or biggest-digit reasoning.
Applies place-value rule with prompts; reverts on edge cases.
Independently applies thousands-first place-value rule. Compares and orders 5+ numbers to 1000 correctly.
Articulates the rule unprompted; orders 7+ numbers including same-hundreds-different-tens close pairs.

rows.expectation_text: round whole numbers to the nearest ten or hundred, in various contexts

levels.descriptor: Cannot apply the 5-or-more rule consistently.
Rounds to nearest 10 with prompts; struggles with nearest 100.
Rounds to nearest 10 AND nearest 100 correctly. Applies the right digit (ones for 10, tens for 100).
Extends to nearest 1000; uses rounding in real-life estimation contexts.

rows.expectation_text: count to 1000, including by 50s, 100s, and 200s, using a variety of tools and strategies

levels.descriptor: Counts by 5s and 10s only; cannot extend to 50s/100s/200s.
Counts by 50s and 100s with prompts; loses track on 200s.
Counts to 1000 by 50s, 100s, AND 200s starting from 0.
Counts by 50s/100s/200s starting from any multiple; uses skip-counting in real-life contexts.

rows.expectation_text: use place value when describing and representing multi-digit numbers in a variety of ways, including with base ten materials

levels.descriptor: Cannot describe multi-digit numbers using place-value language.
Describes hundreds, tens, ones with prompts; misses thousands or zero placeholders.
Describes any number to 1000 in multiple representations: numerals, expanded form, base-ten blocks, place-value chart.
Volunteers regrouping representations (e.g., 347 = 3H+4T+7O = 2H+14T+7O); explains the placeholder role of 0.

rows.expectation_text: use drawings to represent, solve, and compare the results of fair-share problems that involve sharing up to 20 items among 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, and 10 sharers

levels.descriptor: Cannot share fairly when the share doesn't divide evenly.
Shares fairly when divides evenly; struggles with mixed-number leftovers.
Shares up to 20 items fairly with up to 10 sharers; matches fraction to sharer count; writes mixed numbers.
Lists all factor pairs of a dividend; volunteers shares with multiple cuts; explains the matching rule unprompted.

rows.expectation_text: represent and solve fair-share problems that focus on determining and using equivalent fractions, including problems that involve halves, fourths, and eighths; thirds and sixths; and fifths and tenths

levels.descriptor: Cannot recognise that fractions like 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent.
Recognises 1/2 = 2/4 with overlay demo; doesn't yet generalise to other equivalences.
Recognises 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8, 1/3 = 2/6, 1/5 = 2/10 with strips/overlays. Writes equations.
Articulates the multiplication pattern (a/b = (a×N)/(b×N)); generalises to other equivalences (e.g., 2/3 = 4/6 = 6/9).

summative_rubric.usage_notes: Apply this rubric to each child's combined evidence. The level achieved is the LOWEST of the relevant evidence sources for that expectation.

summative_task_script.title: Lesson 5 Summative Task — Equivalent Fractions
summative_task_script.purpose: End-of-unit summative assessment. Captures evidence for B1.7 explicitly.
administration_steps: Bring children back to the carpet after rotations on Day 5.
Hold up the worksheet and walk through the four parts.
Distribute one worksheet per child. Allow 15 minutes.
Score against rubric: 9-10/10 = L4; 7-8 = L3; 5-6 = L2; 0-4 = L1.
summative_task_script.scoring_guidance: Part 1 (3 chains, score out of 3): captures B1.7 baseline. Part 2 (3 pizza shadings, score out of 3): captures B1.7 visual. Part 3 (6 true/false claims, score out of 3): captures B1.7 reasoning. Part 4 (open prompt, score out of 1): captures depth.
